model.demand: 440 volume in each closed direction x divert share; x st130 share onto st130 in the same direction, the rest onto the western route
model.bottleneck: per route, direction and hour the station with the highest existing volume (bottleneck_by_hour); its speed applies to the whole route

pc_conversion.P_T: existing traffic: the bottleneck's heavy_share; diverted traffic: 440's heavy_share

speed.measured_part: speed_volume_curve of the bottleneck direction at min(flow, its last bin's upper edge), veh/h, linear between bin midpoints
speed.assumed_part: minus 0.0125 km/h per pc/h of two-way flow above the measured range: this direction's flow above the last bin plus the traffic added to the opposite direction

model.two_way_cap_rule: when the two-way pc flow exceeds 3,200, each direction's capacity is its share of the two-way demand x 3,200 (assumption)

breakdown.text: if flow breaks down: ~40 km/h (Summala et al. 1986)

queue.label: modelled (simple queue)
queue.queue_end_of_hour: (demand - capacity) x 1 h, in the capacity's unit

model.extra_trip_time: detour length / bottleneck speed - vt3 length / 440 light-traffic speed + average queue delay

measured: hourly volumes and heavy-vehicle shares, light-traffic speeds, 99th percentile and highest 5-min flows, the speed-volume curves up to their last bin (LAM raw)
assumed: st130 speed above the measured range (HCM 2000 slope)
the default split (all on the shortest detour)
the bottleneck speed for the whole route
the simple queue (no carry-over between hours)
that the traffic counted at 440 is the traffic to divert (vt9 shares vt3 at 440; no origin-destination data)

speed_limit_effect.source: Gold v2 sign-change comparisons, analysis week 2026-09-23 .. 10-01: 520 event-group directions, effect minus control station, 15-minute windows before and after the change, errors clustered by zone (analysis/03_scenario_export.py)

dry.unit: km/h of speed change per km/h of limit change

wet.unit: km/h of speed change per km/h of limit change

speed_per_kmh.model: mean_speed ~ limit_change + limit_change:dry + dry + pre_trend_diff + hour period dummies (day 9-15 is the reference); limit_change = new - old km/h
speed_per_kmh.note: Adjusted for the pre-existing trend and the time of day.

lowered.unit: veh/h (effect minus control, after minus before)

raised.unit: veh/h (effect minus control, after minus before)

per_kmh.unit: veh/h per km/h of limit change (new - old)
per_kmh.model: volume effect ~ limit_change, OLS, errors clustered by zone (no other terms)

speed_limit_effect.where_measured: vt3 / other main roads with variable speed-limit signs (not st130); applying it to st130 is an assumption

sources.used_for: capacity low (1,200 veh/h) and mid (1,500 veh/h); breakdown speed about 40 km/h
sources.text: Summala H., Hietamäki J., Lehikoinen A., Tottola K. (1986) Highway capacity and travel speeds on long distances (Tien välityskyky ja matkanopeudet pitkillä tieosilla). Helsinki Traffic Research Unit, issue 7. Two-lane main roads in southern Finland, registration-plate method: with-flow hourly volume and mean travel speed linear up to 1,500 veh/h; at higher demand a 'stable unstable' flow of about 1,200 veh/h at about 40 km/h.

sources.used_for: capacity high (1,700 pc/h per direction) and the two-way cap (3,200 pc/h)
sources.text: Highway Capacity Manual 2000 (TRB), two-lane highways: 1,700 pc/h per direction, 3,200 pc/h both directions combined on extended sections. Cited from secondary sources (FHWA HPMS Field Manual appendix N; Purdue CE361 two-lane worksheet); the HCM text itself was not consulted. One paper cites 3,400 pc/h two-way instead.

sources.used_for: the speed-flow slope above the measured curve
sources.text: HCM 2000 two-lane average travel speed ATS = FFS - 0.00776 vp - fnp (mi/h, vp in pc/h, both directions), as given in FHWA Traffic Analysis Toolbox Vol. VI; 0.00776 mi/h = 0.0125 km/h per pc/h.

HCM 2000 passenger-car equivalents for trucks on two-lane highways, average travel speed, level terrain: 1.7 at 0-600 pc/h, 1.2 at >600-1,200 pc/h, 1.1 at >1,200 pc/h two-way; fHV = 1 / (1 + P_T (E_T - 1)). As given in the FHWA HPMS Field Manual appendix N. Buses are counted as trucks (no separate E_R used).

Digitraffic TMS (LAM) raw data format: 1 car or van, 2 truck without trailer, 3 bus, 4 semi-trailer truck, 5 truck with trailer, 6 car or van with trailer, 7 car or van with trailer or camper, 8 motorcycle or moped, 9 high capacity truck.

caveats: No closure of vt3 at 440 was observed in April-September 2026: nothing here is calibrated on a real closure.
The western route (mt303 / st190) has no usable LAM station: tms 20402 (st190 Viiala) has 9 days, mostly faulty.
The local bypass of option b has no counts.
Road directions of 440, 433 and 402 are not in road_point; northbound / southbound come from the station's municipality names.
